answer: No patient-volume group shows a statistically significant difference (p<0.05) in COVID-19 severity between BCG vaccination and placebo under the chi-square analysis. In the main analysis (subject-level worst COVID-19 AESEV, 4-level severity × arm chi-square, Fisher exact on the collapsed severe vs mild/moderate 2x2 where cells were sparse), the unadjusted p-values were: 1-50 group p=0.171 (chi-square 4-level p=0.264), 51-100 group p=0.364 (chi-square p=0.375), >100 group p=1.000 (chi-square p=0.403) — none significant, and none significant after Holm adjustment. The RTI sensitivity check confirmed this (closest: 1-50 group Fisher p=0.065). If a single group must be named as the near-significant candidate, it is the 1-50 patient volume group, where the direction of effect favors BCG (fewer severe COVID-19 events: 11/61 BCG vs 4/48 placebo on the collapsed 2x2) and the RTI sensitivity reaches p=0.065 — borderline, but not below the p<0.05 threshold.
